## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1) is the opening text of the *Mahāniddesa*, an early canonical commentary preserved within the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. It provides an elaborate, word-by-word doctrinal exegesis of the *Kāmasutta* (Snp 4.1), the first poem of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* [SuttaCentral]. In secondary scholarship, citations of "Nidd 1" frequently denote the first volume of the Pali Text Society edition of the *Mahāniddesa* rather than this individual sutta-exposition; however, specific doctrinal expositions belonging to this text are cited for their definitions of core psychological categories [Norman 1997-2001; Perez-Remon 1980]. Among these, the text defines three types of detachment (*viveka*): bodily detachment (*kāyaviveka*), mental detachment (*cittaviveka*), and detachment from the substrates of existence (*upadhiviveka*) [Norman 1997-2001]. It also treats contact (*phassa*) through the standard formula of impermanence, suffering, alien nature, and non-self [Perez-Remon 1980], and illustrates the perfection of energy (*viriya*) in destroying defilements via the parable of two cities—the city of bandits and the city of peace [Boriharnwanaket].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral connect passages in the *Kāmasuttaniddesa* with other chapters of the *Mahāniddesa* (Mnd 2, Mnd 10, Mnd 14, Mnd 16), the *Cullaniddesa* (Cnd 5, Cnd 6, Cnd 8, Cnd 17, Cnd 22, Cnd 23), and the Abhidhamma *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (*Dukanikkhepa*, Ds 2.3.2) [SuttaCentral]. Computationally, DharmaNexus identifies 3,371 Pali-internal text reuse matches across 185 texts, heavily concentrated in the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), and the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, alongside shared passages in the *Saḷāyatana Saṁyutta* (SN 35) and *Aṅguttara Nikāya* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus indicate textual correspondence with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises, including the *Yogācārabhūmi* (D4035), Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā*, Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
